source.title: KNAS: Green Neural Architecture Search
source.authors: Jing-Jing Xu; Liang Zhao; Jun-Yang Lin; Rundong Gao; Xu Sun; Hong-Xia Yang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether an initialization-time gradient feature correlates with downstream optimization metrics, but does not test whether the listed claim versions hold. Its benchmark results report selected models' validation or test accuracy, not near-zero training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports MGM correlations with training loss and validation or test accuracy. These are proxy correlations, not results showing that the listed networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error. Its theoretical discussion of convergence and its cited results are not empirical outcomes for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests an initialization-time gradient proxy for ranking architectures. Its correlations with downstream loss and accuracy do not establish near-zero training classification error or compare the width, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability, or normalization effects specified in V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that MGM provides a useful architecture-evaluation proxy and that KNAS achieves substantial search speedups with competitive image-classification accuracy, with further improvements over RoBERTA-large on two text-classification tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates architectures without training using initialization-time MGM, then trains selected candidates; it does not test the claim's training-to-zero-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper describes different settings for its image benchmark (Kaiming initialization, CNN cells, batch normalization) and text tasks (Xavier initialization, self-attention cells, layer normalization), but does not report these as controlled comparisons of training error.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization-time MGM correlates positively with negative training loss and validation accuracy on CIFAR100; Figure 4 also shows qualitative correlations with test accuracy on CIFAR100 and ImageNet-16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MGM can serve as a coarse proxy for downstream architecture performance within the tested NAS-Bench-201 settings.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 139, 2021
record.problems: The reported correlations are aggregate proxy relationships and do not provide training classification-error values. Figures 4(a) and 4(b) give no precise correlation coefficients in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Table 2 report selected architectures' validation or test accuracies and search times, not training classification error; they were omitted. Theoretical convergence statements and results cited from other papers were also omitted as they are not empirical outcomes for the listed versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels; effects of size, early stopping, and regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched initialization on learning speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep convolutional training.
Recovery or divergence around learning-rate stability thresholds and sharpness dynamics during training.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Using Kaiming initialization and batch normalization in image experiments, and Xavier initialization and layer normalization in text experiments, supplies no controlled test of V4 or V6. The quadratic-loss convergence argument concerns gradient Gram matrices rather than any listed claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error, including with corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of student width.
Depth, identity shortcuts, special initialization for plain networks, and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and training very deep plain networks.
Training behavior above stability thresholds, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.note: Reported as an aggregate correlation across experiments; the paper does not give individual architecture training-error results here.
rows.check: The approximately 0.53 correlation is correctly recorded for negative training loss. It gives neither absolute training loss nor training classification error and therefore cannot establish V1.
